clue.text: If at first you don't succeed, try …

definitions.text: If at first you don't succeed, try …

parts.words: If at first you don't succeed, try …
parts.note: the proverb ends 'try, try again', but here the dots invite the fallback scheme you turn to when the first one fails

explanation.walkthrough: The familiar proverb sets you up to complete it with 'again'; the clue instead wants the name for a second scheme kept in reserve.
explanation.definitionFit: A backup scheme adopted after the first approach fails is exactly what the proverb's 'try' leads to.

clue.text: Destructive act to a box office in theatre

indicators.note: in places the earlier pieces within the word for theatre

parts.note: the stage stands for the theatre as a profession

explanation.surface: A vandal wrecks the ticket office at a playhouse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Box office' looks like part of the theatre scene but is just its abbreviation, slipped in after the first letter of the stage.
explanation.definitionFit: Sabotage is deliberate damage or disruption, a destructive act.

clue.text: Listen to endless organ

indicators.note: endless means the organ's word loses its final letter

parts.note: the heart is a bodily organ

explanation.surface: Pay attention to an organ that never stops playing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Organ' suggests the musical instrument, but it is the body part; 'endless' drops its last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: To hear something is to listen to it, a direct synonym.

clue.text: What student has to do without to finish?

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so the word for vying wraps the student

parts.note: to do battle or vie is to compete
L is the learner driver's plate, standing for a student

explanation.surface: What must a student go without in order to finish the course?
explanation.walkthrough: 'Without' reads as lacking, but it means outside: COMPETE goes around L.
explanation.definitionFit: To complete is to bring to an end, a synonym of to finish.

clue.text: Port in the Antipodes (South Australia in short)

indicators.note: in signals the letters lie inside the word Antipodes

parts.note: SA is the short form for the state of South Australia

explanation.surface: A harbour in the southern hemisphere, abbreviated as South Australia.
explanation.walkthrough: The bracket looks like a gloss on where the port is, but it supplies the state's abbreviation. The port is on the Black Sea, nowhere near Australia.
explanation.definitionFit: Odessa is a major Black Sea port city in Ukraine.

clue.text: Forces to dish up mostly frozen confections

indicators.note: mostly means the verb for dishing up loses its last letter

parts.note: to serve food is to dish it up
ices are frozen desserts

explanation.surface: An instruction to serve up a dish made largely of ice cream.
explanation.walkthrough: SERV (SERVE shortened by 'mostly') plus ICES.
explanation.definitionFit: The services are the armed forces: army, navy and air force.

clue.text: Programme of concern for the elderly and infirm

parts.note: Age Concern is a British charity for older people, so the first half of its name is the word for the elderly's concern

indicators.note: infirm, being weak and unsteady, signals the word and is shaken into a new order

explanation.surface: A scheme of care for old and sick people.
explanation.walkthrough: Age Concern was a well-known British charity for older people; take AGE from it. 'Infirm' scrambles AND into NDA.
explanation.definitionFit: An agenda is a list or programme of items to be dealt with.

clue.text: Provision in 9 about a hermit entertaining taking a partner

indicators.note: entertaining means holding as a guest, so the hermit's word takes in the partnering word
about means going round, so the hermit's word is placed around the A

parts.note: a hermit is a recluse
pairing is taking a partner

explanation.surface: A clause in a lease concerning a hermit who has guests and takes a partner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'About' wraps the hermit round A; 'entertaining' then takes the partnering word in after the first two letters. 9 is LEASEHOLD, so the provision is in a lease.
explanation.definitionFit: A repairing clause is the provision in a lease setting out who must carry out repairs.

clue.text: Conveyance running to time

parts.note: conveyance suggests transport keeping to a timetable, but here it is a legal transfer of property that lasts for a fixed term

explanation.walkthrough: A train or bus running on time is the false picture; the conveyance is a property transfer limited to a term of years.
explanation.definitionFit: Tenure of property under a lease for a fixed period is a legal grant that runs out at a set date.

clue.text: American symbol reflecting composer, almost English

indicators.note: reflecting, as in a mirror, means the pieces are read backwards
almost means the composer's name loses its final letter

parts.note: Edward Elgar was an English composer

explanation.surface: An American emblem mirrors an English composer, nearly.
explanation.walkthrough: ELGA (Elgar, 'almost') plus E gives ELGAE, which 'reflecting' turns round.
explanation.definitionFit: The bald eagle is the national bird and emblem of the United States.

clue.text: Matured back to front to give one a lift

indicators.note: back to front means the final letter of the phrase is shifted to the front

parts.note: fruit that matured got ripe

explanation.surface: Something aged that is reversed gives you a boost.
explanation.walkthrough: GOT RIPE has its last letter, E, moved to the front.
explanation.definitionFit: An ego trip is self-indulgent activity that boosts one's self-esteem, a lift to the ego.

clue.text: Almost rescue a girl in open country

indicators.note: almost means the word for rescue loses its last letter

parts.note: to save is to rescue
Anna is a girl's name

explanation.surface: Nearly rescuing a young woman out on the plains.
explanation.walkthrough: SAV (SAVE, 'almost') plus ANNA.
explanation.definitionFit: A savanna is a grassy plain with few trees, open country.

clue.text: Well dressed beef

definitions.meaning: an old word for cattle, the animals that give beef

explanation.walkthrough: The old word for cattle survives in neatsfoot oil.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both trim in appearance and, archaically, oxen or cattle.

clue.text: Dances madly at musical to give one a lift

indicators.note: madly signals the dancing letters are thrown into a wild new order

parts.note: Hair is a famous 1960s rock musical

explanation.surface: People dance wildly at a show to cheer someone up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Madly' rearranges DANCES into SEDANC; 'at' joins it to HAIR.
explanation.definitionFit: A sedan chair was an enclosed seat carried on poles, literally lifting its passenger.

clue.text: Leading Tesco cereal product is sticky-sweet

indicators.note: leading means the first letter of the supermarket's name
product suggests the result of working the word cereal into another form

explanation.surface: A supermarket's own cereal brand is cloyingly sweet.
explanation.walkthrough: T plus CEREAL rearranged ('product') into REACLE. Tesco is a large British supermarket chain.
explanation.definitionFit: Treacle is a thick sticky syrup, the sticky-sweet stuff itself.

clue.text: Rank altar cloth

definitions.meaning: the linen cloth on which the bread and wine are placed at Mass

explanation.walkthrough: The church sense is less familiar than the army one.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a non-commissioned army rank and a liturgical linen cloth.

clue.text: It's a fun sort of material

indicators.note: sort as a verb means to arrange, so the letters of the phrase are put in another order

explanation.surface: A remark that some fabric is rather enjoyable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sort of' rearranges ITSAFUN.
explanation.definitionFit: Fustian is a thick hard-wearing cotton fabric such as corduroy.

clue.text: Thrive on fine meal, his cooking

parts.note: flour is finely ground meal

indicators.note: cooking means being worked up, so the letters of his are mixed

explanation.surface: Doing well on his home-cooked fine food.
explanation.walkthrough: FLOUR plus HIS mixed up ('cooking') into ISH.
explanation.definitionFit: To flourish is to grow vigorously and prosper.

clue.text: Met one GP in ten to resolve a skin problem

indicators.note: in places the mixed letters inside the figures for ten

parts.note: ten written as figures, 1 and 0, looks like IO

indicators.note: to resolve means to break up and recombine, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Meeting a family doctor among ten patients to treat a rash.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ten' written in figures, 1 and 0, is read as the letters I and O; 'to resolve' scrambles the other pieces, which sit between them.
explanation.definitionFit: Impetigo is a contagious bacterial skin infection.

clue.text: Nation ever turns to worship?

indicators.note: turns means the letters change their order

explanation.surface: A country always takes to worship, the clue wonders.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turns' rearranges NATIONEVER.
explanation.definitionFit: Veneration is deep reverence or worship.

clue.text: Bipolar disorder ever included with apprehension

indicators.note: included means the jumbled letters are put inside the two poles

parts.note: the two poles are north and south, N and S

indicators.note: disorder signals the following word's letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A mental condition comes with anxiety.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bipolar disorder' looks like a medical term; 'Bipolar' gives the two poles and 'disorder' scrambles the next word, which sits between them.
explanation.definitionFit: Nerves are a feeling of anxious apprehension.

clue.text: To be up-to-date means to go without conclusion

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so the word for a go wraps the conclusion

parts.note: to have a go is to try
a conclusion is an end

explanation.surface: Staying fashionable means never stopping.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Without conclusion' reads as endless, but 'without' is used in its old sense of outside.
explanation.definitionFit: Trendy means fashionable and current, up-to-date.

clue.text: Beowulf, say, needs putting in the picture

indicators.note: needs putting in suggests the answer is set inside the words that follow

explanation.surface: To understand Beowulf you must be briefed first.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Putting in the picture' looks like the idiom for informing; the answer sits inside 'thE PICture'.
explanation.definitionFit: Beowulf is the Old English heroic poem, an example of an epic.

clue.text: Cooked supper containing nothing mean

indicators.note: containing means the jumbled meal holds the zero inside
cooked means the letters are mixed up

parts.note: nothing is zero, shaped like O

explanation.surface: A prepared evening meal with nothing in it is stingy.
explanation.walkthrough: SUPPER rearranged ('Cooked') into PURPSE, with O inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Purpose and mean (as a verb, intend) share the sense of intention.

clue.text: Attaboy! Last comes first in water event

indicators.note: last comes first means the final part moves to the front

parts.note: read as atta plus boy, with boy giving the name Reg

explanation.surface: Cheering a winner at a race on the water.
explanation.walkthrough: Split 'Attaboy' into ATTA and boy, which is REG; moving REG to the front gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A regatta is a series of boat races, a water event.

clue.text: A fool uses energy at work

parts.note: go means energy or vigour
op, short for opus, is a work

explanation.surface: A fool uses up energy on the job.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Uses' and 'at' link GO and OP.
explanation.definitionFit: Goop is an informal word for a silly or foolish person.

clue.text: Back to a time where it all happens

indicators.note: back means the pieces are read in reverse

parts.note: an is a form of the indefinite article
an era is a period of time

explanation.surface: Returning to a period when everything was going on.
explanation.walkthrough: AN ERA read backwards ('Back').
explanation.definitionFit: An arena is the scene of action or activity, where events take place.

clue.text: Setter mistakenly missing turn, goes without nothing but throws up

indicators.note: mistakenly suggests the setter's letters are put in a wrong order
missing means the setter's name loses a letter

parts.note: the setter of this puzzle is Gordius
U as in U-turn

indicators.note: without means the letter for nothing is taken out

parts.note: nothing is zero, shaped like O

explanation.surface: The puzzle-maker, wrongly skipping a turn, goes without and is sick.
explanation.walkthrough: The setter is Gordius; 'missing' drops U to give GORDIS, which 'mistakenly' turns into DISGOR. GOES 'without' O gives GES.
explanation.definitionFit: To disgorge is to discharge or vomit, to throw up.
